title: Practitioner Exam
description: A fixed 40-question exam drawn at random from a 50-question bank covering all six modules. Pass mark is 80%. This is an open-book exam — take your time, browse any module to refresh your memory, or ask the AI assistant for help. Your answers are saved as you go, so leaving the page to look something up is fine. Explanations show after submission so you can learn from any answers you missed.

questions.scenario: Business users keep asking IT to write SQL for every new report because the database table and column names are cryptic.
questions.prompt: What does Pentaho Metadata Editor (PME) provide to solve this?
options: A faster SQL editor for IT
A business-friendly semantic layer that maps tables/columns to business terms so users build reports without SQL
questions.explanation: PME builds a semantic (metadata) layer that translates technical structures into business language, letting non-technical users create reports without writing SQL.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.prompt: A PME metadata domain consists of which two key components?
options: The physical layer (technical structure) and the business model layer (business-oriented view)
A fact table and a dimension table
A JDBC driver and a report template
questions.explanation: A domain has a physical layer (connections, physical tables/columns) and a business model layer that abstracts it into business terms, plus the business view.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: A DBA renames some technical columns in the source database.
questions.prompt: How does the metadata layer reduce disruption to existing reports?
options: It acts as a buffer — as long as the business layer stays consistent, reports keep working despite physical changes
It locks the database against changes
questions.explanation: The metadata layer buffers business users from technical changes, minimising disruption and maintenance as long as the business model remains consistent.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.prompt: What happens to metadata defined on a physical column when a business column references it?
options: The business column inherits the physical column's metadata, property by property, until it overrides a property
The business column must redefine every property manually
questions.explanation: PME uses metadata inheritance: business objects inherit physical metadata per-property unless and until the business object overrides that property.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — Overview

questions.prompt: Who consumes the metadata domains that PME publishes?
options: Pentaho reporting tools, so business users build ad-hoc reports in business terms
questions.explanation: Published domains become data sources for Pentaho reporting tools (e.g. Interactive Reporting), enabling business-term ad-hoc reporting.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.prompt: Which capabilities does PME add on top of raw database access? (Select all that apply.)
options: Business-friendly names and consistent formatting rules
Security controls over which data users can see
Localization that adapts presentation to users' regional settings
Automatic indexing of the source database
questions.explanation: PME provides friendly naming/formatting, security, and localization. It does not index the underlying database.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a PME metadata domain?
options: To create a semantic layer that makes complex database structures accessible while maintaining consistency and security
questions.explanation: The domain's purpose is a semantic layer that makes data accessible to business users while keeping consistency and security across the organisation.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.prompt: The physical layer of a domain encompasses which objects?
options: Connections, physical tables, and physical columns
questions.explanation: The physical layer holds the database connections, physical tables, and physical columns that mirror the source database.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — Overview (Physical Layer)

questions.prompt: What is the rule about connections within a single business model?
options: A model can mix tables from any number of connections
A business model must reference one and only one connection
A model needs at least two connections
Connections are not used by business models
questions.explanation: Each business model references exactly one connection — you cannot mix physical tables from two different connections in the same model.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — Overview (Physical Layer)

questions.prompt: What do relationships (joins) defined between business tables enable?
options: They let PME automatically generate the correct SQL joins when users build reports
questions.explanation: Relationships describe how business tables join, so PME can construct accurate cross-table SQL automatically during report generation.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — Overview (Relationships)

questions.prompt: What is the role of the Business View and its categories?
options: To store the physical database connection
To expose a curated, business-friendly set of columns organised into logical categories for report builders
To define the star schema joins
questions.explanation: The business view is the user-facing layer; categories group related business columns into intuitive collections that match business thinking.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — Overview (Business View)

questions.scenario: You import the Steel Wheels SampleData connection into a new domain.
questions.prompt: Roughly how many physical tables does the SteelWheels physical layer contain?
questions.explanation: The SteelWheels sample data imports 13 interconnected tables spanning customers, products, orders, employees, and financial data.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — SteelWheels

questions.scenario: You need a Total measure that doesn't exist as a column in the physical tables.
questions.prompt: How can you create it in PME?
options: You cannot — only existing columns are allowed
Create a calculated column based on an expression such as [QUANTITYORDERED]*[PRICEEACH]
questions.explanation: PME supports calculated columns derived from an expression over other columns (referenced as [COLUMN]), e.g. Total = [QUANTITYORDERED]*[PRICEEACH].
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — SteelWheels

questions.prompt: Which aggregation options can be set on a numeric column?
questions.explanation: A measure column can be aggregated as Sum, Average, Minimum, or Maximum, set on the column's metadata.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — SteelWheels

questions.scenario: You open the Properties Editor for an object and see prefixes like PT, PC, BT, BC, and CT.
questions.prompt: What do these prefixes indicate?
options: Object types: Physical Table, Physical Column, Business Table, Business Column, and Category
questions.explanation: PME prefixes identify the object: PT (Physical Table), PC (Physical Column), BT (Business Table), BC (Business Column), CT (Category).
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — SteelWheels

questions.scenario: You're building the OrdersME domain from scratch against SampleData.
questions.prompt: What is the first thing you must establish before importing tables?
options: A database connection (with the JDBC driver in place) in the physical layer
questions.explanation: You install the JDBC driver and create a database connection first, then import physical tables and columns from it.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — OrdersME

questions.prompt: After designing the OrdersME business model and view, how do you make it available to report builders?
options: Publish the domain to the Pentaho Server as an XMI file
questions.explanation: The domain is published to the Pentaho Server as an XMI file, where it becomes a data source for Interactive Reporting.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — OrdersME (Publish)

questions.prompt: How do you validate that a published metadata domain works for end users?
options: Read the XMI file by hand
Create an Interactive Report against the domain in the User Console
questions.explanation: You test the domain by building an Interactive Report that leverages the semantic layer — proving the metadata bridges database to end-user reporting.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — OrdersME (Test)

questions.scenario: In a star schema, your ORDERFACT table joins out to the Customers, Products, and Time dimensions.
questions.prompt: Which relationship cardinality models these fact-to-dimension joins?
options: Many-to-one (N:1) from the fact table to each dimension
questions.explanation: Many fact rows reference one dimension row, so the relationships from ORDERFACT to each dimension are N:1 (many-to-one), typically inner joins.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — OrdersME (Relationships)

questions.prompt: What is the Query Builder used for?
options: Assembling and previewing a query against a business model to validate it before publishing
questions.explanation: Query Builder lets you select business columns, apply constraints, and preview results — validating the model's relationships and columns.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — Query Builder

questions.prompt: Why might you create more than one business table that references the same physical table?
options: For scenarios like applying different security or filtering to the same underlying data
questions.explanation: PME lets multiple business tables (and columns) reference one physical table — useful for filtering, security, or alternate views of the same data.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Domains & Models — Overview (Business Tables)

questions.scenario: You create the OrderStarCustomer business model and notice a system-generated ID at the top of its properties.
questions.prompt: What should you do with the BV_MODEL_1 id?
options: Leave it unchanged — PME uses it internally to reference the model when generating SQL
questions.explanation: BV_MODEL_1 is the model's internal unique ID used for SQL generation; you should not change it.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — OrderStarCustomer

questions.prompt: When adding business tables to a model, how are they added?
options: All at once as a group
Individually — by dragging each physical table from the connection into Business Tables
Automatically when the model is created
questions.explanation: Tables must be dragged in individually (not as a group); each prompts a Business Model Properties dialog showing its IDs.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — OrderStarCustomer (Business Tables)

questions.prompt: A business table dragged from PT_PRODUCTS gets which kind of ID?
options: BT_PRODUCTS_PRODUCTS, keeping a reference to the physical table PT_PRODUCTS
A random UUID with no link to the physical table
questions.explanation: The business table gets an ID like BT_PRODUCTS_PRODUCTS and keeps a reference to its physical table (PT_PRODUCTS) for inheritance.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — OrderStarCustomer (Business Tables)

questions.scenario: You're wiring up the OrderStarCustomer star schema.
questions.prompt: Which relationships connect ORDERFACT to the dimensions?
options: N:1 (many-to-one) inner joins — ORDERFACT→CUSTOMER_W_TER via CUSTOMERNUMBER, →PRODUCTS via PRODUCTCODE, →DIM_TIME via TIME_ID
No joins — the tables are independent
questions.explanation: Three N:1 inner-join relationships form the star: ORDERFACT to CUSTOMER_W_TER (CUSTOMERNUMBER), PRODUCTS (PRODUCTCODE), and DIM_TIME (TIME_ID).
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — OrderStarCustomer (Relationships)

questions.prompt: In what order does metadata flow through the layers?
options: Physical → business model → business view (each inheriting from the previous)
There is no inheritance between layers
questions.explanation: Metadata enriched on physical objects is inherited by business objects, which is then exposed through the business view — overridable at each level.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — Overview

questions.prompt: How does overriding inherited metadata work in PME?
options: Overriding one property replaces all inherited metadata
Each property can be overridden individually; un-overridden properties keep inheriting
Overrides only apply to physical columns
questions.explanation: Inheritance operates property-by-property: a business object overrides specific properties while still inheriting the rest.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — Overview

questions.scenario: You want a single 'Contact Name' field that combines first and last name.
questions.prompt: How do you create it?
options: Create a calculated business column with an expression that concatenates the name columns
questions.explanation: A calculated business column defined by an expression (concatenating the name columns) produces a derived Contact Name field.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — OrderStarCustomer (Properties)

questions.prompt: In the OrderStarCustomer business view, columns are grouped into categories such as…
questions.explanation: The business view organises business columns into logical categories (Orders, Customers, Products, Time) that mirror business thinking.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — OrderStarCustomer (Business Views)

questions.prompt: Which connection does the OrderStarCustomer model reference?
questions.explanation: The model is linked to the hsqldb:sampledata connection (the Steel Wheels sample database).
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — OrderStarCustomer

questions.prompt: Which statements about business tables/columns are correct? (Select all that apply.)
options: A business table references a physical table and inherits its metadata
Metadata can be enriched (friendly names, formats, aggregation) at the business level
Multiple business tables can reference the same physical table
Business tables must be created before any physical tables exist
questions.explanation: Business tables reference and inherit from physical tables, expose enrichable metadata, and several can reference one physical table. Physical tables must exist first.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Properties — Overview

questions.prompt: What is a metadata Concept in PME?
options: A reusable bundle of metadata properties (formatting, alignment, aggregation, hidden) applied to many columns via inheritance
questions.explanation: A concept packages metadata properties once so they can be applied consistently across many columns through inheritance.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Overview

questions.scenario: You want all financial columns to display the same currency formatting without configuring each one.
questions.prompt: What's the efficient approach?
options: Define a USCurrency concept once and apply it to the columns with Set Parent Concept
Write SQL formatting in each report
questions.explanation: Concepts let you define formatting once and apply it via Set Parent Concept, instantly inheriting the properties — consistent and maintainable.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor

questions.prompt: Which mask does the Number concept use?
questions.explanation: The Number concept uses the mask #,##0 (thousand separators, right-aligned), the base for numeric formatting.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor (Numeric)

questions.prompt: The USCurrency concept is built how?
options: Inheriting from Number, overriding the mask to $#,##0.00;($#,##0.00)
questions.explanation: USCurrency is a child of Number that overrides the mask to $#,##0.00;($#,##0.00), formatting currency with negative-value handling.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor (Currency)

questions.scenario: An internal Employee Number should never appear in report interfaces but must still be a whole number when accessed.
questions.prompt: Which concept handles this?
options: Hidden — a child of ID that sets 'Hidden For the User?'
questions.explanation: The Hidden concept (child of ID) marks the field 'Hidden For the User?', excluding it from report interfaces while keeping whole-number formatting.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor (ID)

questions.prompt: Which mask does the Date concept apply?
questions.explanation: The Date concept standardises date display with the mask MM-dd-yyyy.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor (Date)

questions.prompt: How do you apply a concept to a business column?
options: Drag the column onto the concept
Right-click the column and choose Set Parent Concept, then pick the concept
questions.explanation: Right-clicking a business column and choosing Set Parent Concept assigns the parent concept, and the column inherits its properties.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor (Apply)

questions.scenario: You applied the Date concept to Required Date, but in the report it still isn't formatted as a date.
questions.prompt: What's the most likely reason?
options: The column's data type was left as String, and the Mask for Number or Date only applies to numeric/date types
questions.explanation: The Mask for Number or Date property only takes effect on numeric or date data types; a column still typed as String won't be formatted.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor (Interactive Report)

questions.prompt: Which concepts are defined in the workshop's concept hierarchy? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: The workshop builds Number, USCurrency (child of Number), ID, Hidden (child of ID), and Date. Cube/Dimension are OLAP terms, not PME concepts.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Concepts — Concept Editor

questions.prompt: What does metadata security on a model control?
options: Which roles can access the domain and its tables/columns, enforced at the model layer
questions.explanation: Metadata security restricts table/column/row access by role on the model, enforced once at the model layer so every report inherits it.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Security & Data Access — Overview

questions.scenario: EMEA managers must only see EMEA customers from the same shared model.
questions.prompt: Which feature delivers this?
options: Row-level security via a role-based data constraint (e.g. Territory = 'EMEA')
questions.explanation: Row-level security uses a role-based data constraint to filter rows (Territory = 'EMEA'), so different roles see different rows from the same model.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Security & Data Access — Row-Level Security

questions.prompt: Why is enforcing security in the metadata model preferable to coding it in each report?
options: It is enforced once at the model layer, so every report inherits it consistently
questions.explanation: Model-layer security is defined once and inherited by every report, avoiding inconsistent per-report re-implementation.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Security & Data Access — Overview

questions.scenario: In the workshop, the user SUZY should be restricted while Admin sees everything.
questions.prompt: How is SUZY's restriction defined?
options: By deleting rows from the database
By a role-based data constraint on the business model (her role only returns Territory = 'EMEA' rows)
By giving her the Administrator role
By hiding the whole domain from her
questions.explanation: A role-based data constraint filters rows for SUZY's role to Territory = 'EMEA', while Admin (unconstrained) sees all rows.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Security & Data Access — Row-Level Security

questions.prompt: What must you do after publishing a changed secured model for the change to take effect in reports?
options: Refresh the metadata cache on the Pentaho Server
questions.explanation: As with any published domain change, you refresh the server's metadata cache so the User Console picks up the new model.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Security & Data Access — Row-Level Security

questions.prompt: Metadata security in PME can authorize at which levels?
questions.explanation: The Pentaho metadata model offers table-, column-, and row-level authorization control.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Security & Data Access — Overview

questions.scenario: Your source data lives in MongoDB and the business wants ad-hoc reports on it.
questions.prompt: What is the overall approach in the MongoDB Reports use case?
options: Export MongoDB to Excel and email it
Bring the data in (e.g. via PDI), model it, and build Interactive/Analyzer reports on the resulting data source
Rewrite MongoDB as a relational database manually
questions.explanation: The use case takes a MongoDB source through Pentaho's tooling and exposes it for Interactive/Analyzer reporting.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Use Cases — MongoDB Reports

questions.prompt: Which Pentaho tool is typically used to read and aggregate MongoDB data in this use case?
options: Pentaho Data Integration (PDI) — including a MongoDB aggregation step
questions.explanation: PDI connects to MongoDB (with a MongoDB aggregation/input step) to read and shape the data for downstream reporting.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Use Cases — MongoDB Reports (Data Integration)

questions.prompt: What lets business users build the final reports without touching MongoDB query syntax?
options: A semantic/metadata data source they report against in the User Console
questions.explanation: Once exposed as a Pentaho data source/model, users build reports in business terms in the User Console — no MongoDB query language needed.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Use Cases — MongoDB Reports

questions.prompt: Across the whole course, what is the end-to-end metadata workflow?
options: Connect & import → build business model + relationships → enrich with properties/concepts → secure → publish → report
Install the database → write reports in code
Build a cube → query with MDX
questions.explanation: The PME lifecycle: connect/import physical tables, build the business model and relationships, enrich with properties and concepts, apply security, publish the XMI domain, and report against it.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - ME Practitioner: Use Cases — MongoDB Reports
